column2: Retain the singular he remained and the three-year interval without war between Syria and Israel. The unexpressed subject is not turned into plural they or explicitly identified as the entire country; the previous king narrative supplies the likely reference.
Retain the third year and Jehoshaphat's descent to the king of Israel. Judah and Israel remain distinct titles, and no precise month or independent chronological reconciliation is supplied.

Retain the question about the ownership of Remmath-gilead and the contrast with remaining silent about recovering it. From the hand preserves the control metaphor; the two royal parties are not conflated.

Retain the invitation with us and the three paired comparisons: I/you, my people/your people and my horses/your horses. The English keeps the selected order rather than reversing the formula, and no additional chariots are introduced.

Retain the polite request to inquire of the Lord today. The Greek imperative is plural although addressed to the king; English inquire can cover the king and those acting on his request without supplying a new group.

Retain about four hundred prophets, the alternative of going or holding back, and the doubled giving rendered surely give. It supplies the unexpressed object from the proposed campaign; the king's hands are plural here and no explicit Syrian king is added until verse 12.

Retain Jehoshaphat's negative question and the repeated reference to the Lord. Through him marks the prophet as intermediary; the text does not explicitly deny the title prophet to the earlier four hundred in this sentence.

Retain the remaining one man, the king's hatred, good versus only bad, and Micaiah son of Imlah. Only is supported by the restrictive all' e construction. Jehoshaphat's restrained third-person request remains ordinary human address.

Retain eunuch rather than silently broadening the selected office to a generic messenger. Bring supplies the action in the elliptical Greek command quickly, Micaiah; the named prophet and patronymic remain intact.

Retain each king's own throne and the explicit armed description at Samaria's gates. Robes and a threshing floor are not imported into this selected setting; all the prophets continue prophesying before them.

Retain Zedekiah son of Chenaanah, iron horns made for himself, and the quoted promise of goring Syria until its end. The claim is reported prophetic speech, not editorial endorsement; ordinary you addresses the human king.

Retain the uniform prophetic message, Remmath-gilead, promised success and even the king of Syria delivered into plural hands. The selected third-person future allows the Lord as subject of both grant success and give; it is not changed to an independent second-person promise of prosperity.

Retain Behold, all the prophets, one mouth, and the messenger's two requests that Micaiah conform his words and speak favorably. One of them preserves the singular exemplar within the collective agreement, and no claim of divine authority is added to this pressure.

Retain the oath by the living Lord and the restrictive correspondence between whatever the Lord says and what Micaiah will speak. The repeated Lord is not pronominalized away; this is speech about God, not direct address to Him.

Retain the repeated battle question and Micaiah's initially favorable answer without adding an adverb such as sarcastically. The Lord as subject of success/giving and singular hand differ from nearby phrasing and remain. The unstated object it is supplied from the campaign context.
column3: How should Micaiah's initial favorable response be performed aloud while leaving its irony or rhetorical intention to the narrative rather than an added explanation?

column2: Retain the repeated-adjuration question and speaking truth in the Lord's name. Must interprets the rhetorical force of how many times I adjure you rather than translating a separate necessity verb; no only is inserted before truth.

Retain the opening Not so, all Israel scattered on mountains, the shepherdless flock, and the Lord's no master judgment. Each returning to his own house in peace remains singular distributive; master is human in this image, distinct from the divine speaker.

Retain the king's question to Jehoshaphat and his good/bad contrast about Micaiah. Only is warranted by the restrictive construction; the rebuke remains the king's interpretation, without a narrator's explanation of the prophet's motives.

Retain both Not so statements and not I around the command to hear, rather than deleting the difficult repetitions. The full title Lord, God of Israel, throne, entire heavenly army and both sides remain. Dashes are an editorial attempt to make the interruptions audible, not a solution to the opening syntax.
column3: How do the repeated not so and not I relate syntactically to the king's accusation and Micaiah's following vision?

column2: Retain the Lord's question about deceiving Ahab, his title, the ascent and fall at Remmath-gilead, and varied answers. That he may go expresses the relation of the future clauses to the deception; the intended victim is not replaced by the prophet or army.

Retain an indefinite spirit coming forward, standing before the Lord and volunteering to deceive. By what means naturally expresses en tini; no identity such as Satan or an angel is supplied to the unnamed spirit.

Retain becoming a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets, the Lord's assurance of deception and success, and the two commands to go and act. You addresses the spirit, not God, and the divine agency is not softened into mere prediction or passive permission.

Retain Now behold, the Lord's giving of a lying spirit in all these prophets' mouth, and His declaration of calamities against the king. Put naturally expresses gave in this construction; the narrative's troubling divine agency remains explicit without a theological gloss.

Retain the blow on Micaiah's cheek and the selected question what sort of spirit of the Lord spoke in you. It is not replaced with the familiar question about which way the spirit left the speaker. The name follows the established Zedekiah spelling despite the irregular selected case form.

Retain the presentative, the prediction of seeing on that day, and the inner chamber within an inner chamber for hiding. The nested room image is not compressed into a generic house; the precise architectural force of the genitive remains provisional.

Retain the command to take and return Micaiah to Emer, the city ruler, and the second recipient Joash, the king's son. The sentence deliberately continues into verse 27; no replacement with Amon or a newly supplied speaker occurs.

Retain the order to imprison, bread of affliction and water of affliction, and the king's hoped-for peaceful return. The Greek uses one eating infinitive with both bread and water; the inherited English preserves that awkward coordination rather than silently changing the ration's character.
column3: Would eat bread of affliction and drink water of affliction better preserve the selected zeugma in natural spoken English, with drink explicitly recognized as supplied?

column2: Retain the emphatic conditional return rendered do return and the consequent denial that the Lord has spoken in Micaiah. The selected verse ends here; no hear all peoples sentence is imported from another form of the account.
Retain the ascent of Israel's king with Jehoshaphat to Remmath-gilead. The selected with him is preserved rather than flattening the two kings into an unidentified army.

Retain the first-person concealment and the command that Jehoshaphat put on my clothing, not your clothing. The repeated actual concealment and entry into battle remain; no motive explaining the exchange is supplied.

Retain thirty-two chariot commanders and the prohibition against attacking small and great except the king of Israel. Only is supported by the strong exclusive expression; the ordinary human commands require no divine-address morphology.

Retain the commanders' apparent identification, their surrounding Jehoshaphat to fight, and his cry. The account does not specify the words or recipient of the cry, and no explicit divine rescue statement is added here.
Retain the corrected recognition and the commanders' withdrawal. The negative this was not the king of Israel remains the reason for their turning away, without adding a tactical explanation.

Retain good aim for eustochos, not random shooting, and the selected lung/breastplate description. The king's request to turn the charioteer's hands and remove him from battle, because he is wounded, remains. The anatomical and armor relation is difficult and needs specialist attention before smoothing.
column3: What does between the lung and the thorax denote here: anatomy, armor or their relation; can turn your hands be expressed as a driving command without overexplaining?

column2: Retain the rout, the king standing in the chariot facing Syria from morning to evening, the wound's blood and death in the evening. Both blood clauses remain, including the unusual blood of the rout; they are not collapsed into a single familiar wound account. Hollow follows kolpos provisionally.
column3: Review the relation of the initial battle's rout to the final blood of the rout, and whether hollow best denotes the chariot's interior or floor.

column2: Retain sunset, the army herald standing and the two distributive destinations, each man's own city and land. The quotation continues into verse 37 so that the king's death supplies its stated cause.

Retain for the king is dead inside the herald's announcement, followed by the plural return and burial in Samaria. The selected repeated city name is preserved, and no new agent is supplied for the burial.

Retain the washing at Samaria's spring, both swine and dogs licking blood, and prostitutes bathing in blood. These selected details correspond to the earlier judgment announcement and are not replaced with a sanitized or differently ordered account. The Lord's spoken word remains the stated interpretive frame.

Retain Ahab's remaining acts, all he did, the ivory house and all the cities, then the presentative rhetorical annals reference. Ivory house leaves its construction/material relation unspecified; the English does not claim a building made entirely of ivory.
Retain slept with his fathers and Ahaziah's succession. The death formula is not treated as an alternative to the battle death just narrated; it remains the book's closing royal notice.

Retain both statements of Jehoshaphat's accession and the fourth year of Ahab. The repeated became king is present in the selected text; no attempt is made to reconcile this chronology with the earlier inserted Jehoshaphat account.
Retain age thirty-five, twenty-five years in Jerusalem and Azubah daughter of Selei. This spelling is not harmonized to Gazouba in the earlier notice; the selected royal figures remain unchanged.

Retain all Asa's way, the denial of turning aside and doing right in the Lord's eyes. The positive evaluation is kept alongside the following high-place exception rather than expanded into an assertion of complete cultic reform.

Retain the exception that the high places were not removed and the people's continued sacrifice and incense there. Still represents eti; the selected negative is not altered to match another royal notice.
Retain the explicit peace with the king of Israel. The sentence does not name that king or itself recount a marriage or military agreement, so none is added.

Retain Jehoshaphat's remaining acts, mighty deeds and the presentative annals question. The next stored unit is verse 51 because the selected running text omits 47–50 here; material from the earlier insertion is not duplicated into this gap.

Retain the sleep and burial formulas, beside his fathers, the City of David his father and Joram's succession. Father functions dynastically for David; no biological genealogy is added to explain the title.
Retain Ahaziah son of Ahab, accession in Samaria in Jehoshaphat's seventeenth year, and two years of rule. The selected dates are not adjusted to harmonize with the preceding royal chronology.

Retain the distinct father Ahab and mother Jezebel paths and the sins of Jeroboam's house. Jeroboam's causing Israel to sin remains the closing relative clause; maternal agency in the comparison is not omitted.

Retain plural Baalim and plural them, the Lord's full title, and all that had happened before him. The selected comparison is not replaced with only his father's deeds; provoked preserves the adverse divine response without an added object of anger.
